title: Sherlock Holmes Franchise Overview
body:
Sherlock Holmes is a fictional detective created by British author Arthur Conan Doyle, first appearing in print in 1887, whose stories entered the public domain in most jurisdictions and have been adapted for stage, film, radio and television for over a century.

This public edition records only verifiable facts — story-collection titles, authors, publication years and adaptation dates — in original wording, with no copied passages from Doyle's text.

The companion Signature edition is separate, labeled unofficial fiction with original detectives and cases, and it claims no affiliation with any estate or rights holder.

How to use this record: start with the overview, then read the work-by-work records in publication order. Every date and credit below is a public fact; no copyrighted text is reproduced anywhere in this database.

title: Sherlock Holmes Reading and Viewing Order Guide
body:
Recommended public order for the works in this database is publication and release order, beginning with A Study in Scarlet (1887) and ending with Sherlock Holmes (film) (2009). That order follows how the franchise actually reached the public, and it avoids assuming any later reordering.

The full order is: A Study in Scarlet (1887); The Sign of the Four (1890); The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes (1892); The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes (1894); The Hound of the Baskervilles (1902); The Return of Sherlock Holmes (1905); The Valley of Fear (1915); His Last Bow (1917); The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes (1927); Sherlock Holmes (film) (2009). Each title in that list has its own record in this database with its credited creators and format.

This guide contains facts only. It does not reproduce story text, and it does not claim that any Signature continuation belongs in the official order.
